ops.new_text: All images were generated with the EIDORS toolbox, v3.8 (Adler and Lionheart, 2006) <!--ref:Adler2006EIDORS--><!--anchor:quote:Uses%20and%20abuses%20of%20EIDORS--> on the registered 16-electrode cylinder (adjacent drive and adjacent measurement, 208 voltages per frame; mesh, electrode and geometry parameters in S2 Table) with 3,600 geometries: background 1.0 S/m, two lung inclusions at 0.5 S/m and one heart inclusion at 2.0 S/m, with randomised radii, centres and heterogeneous conductivity. For each geometry three forward and three inverse solves were run (mixed, lung only, heart only): the network's input is the mixed reconstruction and its targets the single-organ reconstructions. Gaussian measurement noise was added to the inhomogeneous voltage frame only, before reconstruction, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 20 dB in the EIDORS convention: the norm of the difference frame divided by the norm of the added noise equals 10, an amplitude ratio. In the single-organ reconstructions the heart image's amplitude is 0.14, 0.085 and 0.099 of the lung image's (training-split SD ratio; GREIT, Gauss–Newton, back-projection), which makes the cardiac component weak in this simulation (S2 Table). The level is fixed and stated because an EIT system's SNR depends on its operating conditions (Gagnon et al., 2010) <!--ref:Gagnon2010TBME--><!--anchor:quote:A%20Resistive%20Mesh%20Phantom%20for%20Assessing%20the%20Performance%20of%20EIT%20Systems-->. Geometries and noise seeds were split 2,880/360/360 into training, validation and test frames, bit-identical across the three reconstructors, so that the datasets differ only in the reconstruction operator.

The second decoder is hard parameter sharing (Caruana, 1997) <!--ref:Caruana1997MTL--><!--anchor:quote:Multitask%20Learning-->. The two L1 losses were summed with fixed weights of 1.0 each, a scope decision: the original study proposed the branch together with a multi-weighted loss and attributed its improvement to their interaction, and this study evaluates the branch alone. Fixed weights are a defensible default, since unit or tuned fixed weights have matched specialised multi-task optimisers in controlled comparisons (Kurin et al., 2022; Xin et al., 2022) <!--ref:Kurin2022Unitary--><!--anchor:quote:In%20Defense%20of%20the%20Unitary%20Scalarization%20for%20Deep%20Multi-Task%20Learning--> <!--ref:Xin2022MTOHelp--><!--anchor:quote:Do%20Current%20Multi-Task%20Optimization%20Methods%20in%20Deep%20Learning%20Even%20Help%3F-->; learned weighting (Kendall et al., 2018) <!--ref:Kendall2018--><!--anchor:quote:Multi-task%20Learning%20Using%20Uncertainty%20to%20Weigh%20Losses--> was not tested. Training settings, fixed before registration: Adam at 1 × 10⁻³ with cosine decay to 1 × 10⁻⁵, batch 16, at most 200 epochs with early stopping on validation loss (patience 20, best weights restored), L1 loss on the float target, no output activation, no augmentation, and one dataset-wide normalisation affine, a fixed location–scale standardisation (subtract the training-split mean, divide by its SD) estimated on that dataset's training split and applied to inputs and targets, referred to below as that dataset's affine. Thirty seeds (0 to 29) per arm and training row were trained on one machine (Mac mini M4, Apple MPS backend; a seed fixes data order and initialisation, but the backend does not guarantee bit-identical re-execution, so a seed defines a replicate rather than an exactly reproducible run); seed-to-seed variability is of the order of the effects at stake (Renard et al., 2020) <!--ref:Renard2020SciRep--><!--anchor:quote:Variability%20and%20reproducibility%20in%20deep%20learning%20for%20medical%20image%20segmentation-->. The GREIT row reuses seeds 0 to 29 of the companion study's 20 dB training (same machine and code; PyTorch 2.8.0), trained between 2026-09-24 16:26 and 2026-09-26 00:44 and scored on 2026-09-26, before the registered state was hashed (17:41); the registered text declares this reuse and names that row as the reference against which the two R1 cells are read (Section 2.5), so a between-campaign difference is confounded with every contrast pairing a GREIT-trained network with one trained here (Section 3.4).

All three signs named in Section 1.1 appeared, on evidence of three standings. Without retraining, a change of reconstructor cost both arms 19 to 34 heart-Dice points even after scale correction (exploratory), and the registered transfer hypothesis was falsified in every cell (registered). With the deployed reconstructor's images in the training pool, pooled training with a per-source affine was never worse than retraining on that reconstructor by more than 0.3 points (first addendum; descriptive). With the deployed reconstructor outside the pool, the same recipe lost 16 to 62 points (an upper bound, Section 2.3), falsified against a margin fixed in advance (second addendum; tested). Fig 5 arranges the remedies tested. Only putting the target reconstructor's images into training recovered the loss; the two ways of doing so differed by −0.08 to +0.36 points with two of six intervals favouring pooling (first addendum; descriptive), a difference this design cannot separate from threefold optimisation steps.

The nearest clinical analogues are a left-ventricle segmentation network that fell by 21 to 31 Dice points, from 0.89–0.91 to 0.60–0.69, when the MRI manufacturer changed (Yan et al., 2020) <!--ref:Yan2020RadiolAI--><!--anchor:quote:Dice%20reduced%20from%2089.7%25--> and cross-institutional tumour segmentation that lost 4 and 17 points, from 0.72 and 0.76 to 0.68 and 0.59 (AlBadawy et al., 2018) <!--ref:AlBadawy2018MedPhys--><!--anchor:quote:dice%20coefficients%3A%200.68%20%C2%B1%200.19%20and%200.59%20%C2%B1%200.19-->; the 16 to 62 points lost here and the exploratory 19 to 34 points are losses of the same kind, but two differences forbid a comparison of magnitudes: in those studies the label is anatomy and only the input changes with the domain; here the reference is the held-out reconstructor's own cardiac image and changes with it, so this study's losses are upper bounds on the input-side generalisation loss. Those studies used patients and manufacturers; this one simulation, three conventional algorithms and thirty seeds.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Forward model | EIDORS v3.8 with Netgen; cylinder of radius 2 and height 2 (model units), 16 electrodes of radius 0.1 in one ring at height 1 (`ng_mk_cyl_models([2,2,maxh],[16,1],[0.1])`), electrode contact impedance 0.01 in model units (the `ng_mk_fwd_model` default); normalised difference data for all three reconstructors (`mdl_normalize`); tetrahedral forward mesh with maximum element size 0.10; adjacent drive and adjacent measurement with current-carrying electrodes excluded (`mk_stim_patterns(16,1,[0,1],[0,1],{'no_meas_current'},1)`), 208 measurements per frame |
| Geometry | 3,600 geometries: background 1.0 S/m; two lung inclusions at 0.5 S/m with radius drawn from U(0.30, 0.60); one heart inclusion at 2.0 S/m with radius drawn independently from U(0.15, 0.30); inclusion centres jittered by ±0.05 around fixed positions; within-organ heterogeneity σ(x) = σ₀(1 + 0.25 f(x)), f the sum of 8 random sinusoids with correlation length 0.60; split 2,880 / 360 / 360 by geometry index, identical for all three reconstructors |
| Noise | Additive white Gaussian noise on the 208 inhomogeneous-frame voltages only (homogeneous reference frame noise-free), scaled so that ‖vᵢ − vₕ‖ / ‖noise‖ = 10^(20/20) = 10 (an amplitude ratio; 20 dB), seed `noise_seed0 + i`, identical across reconstructors |
| GREIT | `mk_GREIT_model` on a coarse cylinder (maximum element size 0.20): 64 × 64 image; 1,000 simulated training targets on the GREITv1 spiral (`distr` 0: radial position 0 to 0.9 of the mesh half-width in equal steps, angle 4321 × that fraction in radians, in the electrode plane, each of radius 0.05 of the mean half-width); desired image the EIDORS default sigmoid of radius 0.2 of the model radius (`GREIT_desired_img_sigmoid`, steepness 10/radius); noise figure 0.5 (nominal) calibrated on one central target of radius 0.02 (`target_size`); realised noise figure on the common reference frame 0.602 |
| One-step Gauss–Newton | `inv_solve_diff_GN_one_step` with `prior_laplace`, parametrised on GREIT's 64 × 64 reconstruction grid through `mk_coarse_fine_mapping` from the same coarse cylinder (no resampling onto the GREIT raster); hyperparameter 0.0016 set by bisection in log₁₀ so that the noise figure (0.607) matches GREIT's realised 0.602 on the common reference frame |
| Back-projection | Sheffield MKI back-projection matrix (`mk_common_gridmdl('backproj')`), 32 × 32 raster, upsampled 2 × 2 by pixel replication (`kron(·, ones(2))`) and masked to GREIT's field of view; no free parameter; noise figure 0.831 on the common reference frame |
| Heart-image amplitude relative to lung-image amplitude (training-split SD ratio of the single-organ reconstructions) | GREIT 0.143; GN 0.085; BP 0.099 |
| Mixed-image amplitude (training-split SD) | GREIT 8.92; GN 0.0555; BP 0.0474 (ratios 161 and 188) |
| Normalisation ("affine") | For each training row one location–scale standardisation estimated on that row's training split (subtract the mean, divide by the SD of all pixels of the mixed images), applied to inputs and targets; fixed, not learned; the pooled rows standardise each source with its own single-source affine before concatenation (per-source affine) |
| Network | U-Net encoder 32-64-128-256 channels, 512-channel bottleneck, two 3 × 3 convolutions with batch normalisation and ReLU per level, 2 × 2 max-pooling; decoders with 2 × 2 transposed convolutions and skip concatenation; D: two decoders of the original width; B_wide: one decoder widened by 1.5312 (48, 96, 192, 392 channels fine to coarse) with two 1 × 1 output heads; parameters D 10,811,298, B_wide 10,743,738 |
